mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and economic growth, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger economic activity, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 2% in the last month
failure_condition: If industrial production growth exceeds 2% but the S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals increased demand in the housing market, which may lead to broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase by more than 5% but the S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) and real federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) suggests a strong labor market and monetary policy alignment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 0.5% and FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25%
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS and FEDFUNDS increase as specified but the S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates economic expansion, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If real GDP growth exceeds 2% but the S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with a low unemployment rate (UNRATE) may indicate tight monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 5% and UNRATE is below 4% but the S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) during a late-cycle expansion may lead to inflation concerns, causing the market to decline and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: If CPI increases by more than 0.5% but the S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) suggests strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If both GDPC1 and INDPRO grow as specified but the S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.
